sn12.32:1.2: Kaḷāra the Aristocrat is otherwise unknown.
sn12.32:1.4: For Phagguna of the Top-Knot, see note on [sn12.12:2.1]().
sn12.32:8.5: Read _khīṇasmiṁ khīṇam’iti_ with PTS and BJT, paralleling the common phrase _vimuttasmiṁ vimuttam’iti_ ([sn12.61:6.2]()). | The syntax here is convoluted: “With the end of that source which is the source of rebirth, I knew regarding that ending, ‘it is ended’.”
sn12.32:12.2: The Buddha focuses in on the topic of feelings. The commentary explains this with reference to the Dīghanakhasutta ([mn74]()), which relates the occasion Sāriputta realized arahantship. The main topic, and the basis for Sāriputta’s insight, was feelings. The Buddha wanted to give Sāriputta the chance to highlight his special domain.
sn12.32:14.9: Variants for _nānussavanti_ are from the roots _sav_ (“flow”) and _sī_ (“lie”). Pali often couples verbs and nouns from the same root for emphasis, and this is probably the case here, “defilements don’t defile”.
sn12.32:16.2: _Pubbe appaṭisaṁviditaṁ_ is an idiom elsewhere used when visiting someone “without letting them know beforehand” ([mn91:26.4](), [an5.50:4.7]()).
